text: Top Vietnamese leader calls for strengthening economic cooperation, investment, and coordination towards APEC 2027

In the framework of the APEC 2026 Leaders' Week in Shenzhen (China), General Secretary and President To Lam of Vietnam held separate meetings with leaders from South Korea, Papua New Guinea, and the Managing Director of the IMF, focusing on expanding bilateral cooperation, macroeconomic stability, and preparations for APEC 2027, according to the Vietnam News Agency.
On the evening of November 18, General Secretary and President To Lam met with South Korean President Lee Jae Myung.

Affirming that Vietnam always values its relationship with South Korea, General Secretary and President To Lam emphasized readiness to promote practical, effective, and comprehensive cooperation across various fields.

President Lee Jae Myung appreciated Vietnam's facilitation for South Korean businesses to invest and operate, resolving outstanding issues, contributing to promoting bilateral economic, trade, and investment relations.

The two leaders agreed to continue deepening the Vietnam-South Korea Comprehensive Strategic Partnership; enhancing cooperation in economics, trade, investment, science and technology, cultural and people-to-people exchanges; and concretizing the commitments and agreements reached.

Later, during the meeting with Papua New Guinea's Prime Minister James Marape on November 19 morning, General Secretary and President To Lam recognized Papua New Guinea's role in the South Pacific region and international forums.
He suggested transforming the good political relations into specific cooperation programs that bring tangible benefits to the people of both countries.

The top Vietnamese leader proposed enhancing delegation exchanges, high-level contacts, promoting diplomatic presence in each other's capitals, effectively implementing signed agreements, including the Memorandum of Understanding on Fisheries Cooperation, while exploring new agreements and establishing bilateral consultation and dialogue mechanisms.

In terms of economics, both sides need to boost cooperation in minerals, oil and gas, processing, forestry, fisheries, infrastructure, telecommunications, energy, labor, and vocational training, the Vietnamese leader said, adding that Vietnam is ready to share agricultural development experiences, welcome Papua New Guinea students for study and vocational training, and improve air connectivity, thus promoting people-to-people exchanges and tourism.

Prime Minister James Marape appreciated Vietnam's economic achievements and expressed a desire to expand cooperation in agriculture, fisheries, forestry, coffee production, and processing, encouraging Vietnamese businesses to explore investment opportunities in Papua New Guinea.
Regarding multilateral cooperation, the two leaders agreed to strengthen coordination at the United Nations and international forums.

The Vietnamese leader emphasized the importance of upholding international law, the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), maintaining peace, stability, maritime safety, and protecting the marine environment.
Vietnam is ready to act as a bridge between ASEAN and the Pacific Islands Forum, the Vietnamese leader noted.
Papua New Guinea also wishes to strengthen ties with ASEAN and act as a bridge between ASEAN and the Pacific island nations, according to Prime Minister James Marape.

In both meetings, General Secretary and President To Lam proposed that South Korea and Papua New Guinea support Vietnam in successfully organizing APEC 2027, and cordially invited the leaders of both countries to attend the APEC 2027 Leaders' Week in Phu Quoc.

President Lee Jae Myung of South Korea and Prime Minister James Marape of Papua New Guinea both affirmed their support for Vietnam hosting APEC 2027, with South Korea being ready to closely coordinate to ensure the event's success.
On November 18, General Secretary and President To Lam met with Ms. Kristalina Georgieva, Managing Director of the International Monetary Fund (IMF).

The General Secretary and President highly valued the IMF's role in maintaining the stability of the international financial and monetary system and promoting global macroeconomic policy coordination; affirming Vietnam's commitment to cooperation with the IMF, especially in policy advice, macroeconomic review, technical support, and capacity building.

Discussing the global economic situation, the General Secretary and President noted that profound changes in order, technology, governance, and development models are creating many risks and uncertainties for the global economy.
As a highly open economy, Vietnam is directly affected by external fluctuations but has gradually improved its resilience and adaptability.
In the first nine months of 2026, Vietnam's GDP grew by over 9% on a stable macroeconomic foundation, continuing to attract interest and investment from major corporations.

The General Secretary and President emphasized Vietnam's determination to enter a new development phase, aiming to become a developed, high-income country by 2045; identifying strategic autonomy linked with deep international integration, with science and technology, innovation, and digital transformation as important foundations and drivers for development.

IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva praised Vietnam's socio-economic achievements and growth prospects, particularly its ability to maintain high growth alongside macroeconomic stability, control inflation, and strengthen major balances of its economy.
According to Ms. Kristalina Georgieva, Vietnam is a model worth referencing in combining rapid growth promotion with maintaining stability and enhancing resilience.
The IMF affirmed its continued support for Vietnam through policy advice, macroeconomic assessment, and technical support in areas where Vietnam has needs.
Both sides agreed to deepen Vietnam-IMF cooperation.

On this occasion, General Secretary and President To Lam cordially invited the Managing Director and IMF experts to participate in activities within the framework of APEC 2027 to be hosted by Vietnam.
